name: South Africa
summary: Table Mountain over Cape Town, Big Five in the Kruger lowveld, the Drakensberg escarpment, two oceans meeting, and eleven official languages.

entries.caption: A World in One Country
entries.description: Table Mountain above a working harbour, wine farms an hour inland, and the Big Five a short flight north.
entries.subject: Table Mountain above Cape Town and the harbour at sunrise

entries.caption: Fynbos and the Garden Route
entries.description: The Cape Floral Kingdom is the smallest and richest of the six on earth, and most of it grows nowhere else.
entries.subject: fynbos and coastline along the Garden Route

entries.caption: The Big Five, Close
entries.description: Kruger and the private Sabi Sands reserves beside it, where the leopards have been watched for generations.
entries.subject: a leopard on a termite mound in the Sabi Sands reserve

entries.caption: Sabi Sands, Off-Road
entries.description: Private traverse means the vehicle can leave the road, which is why the sightings are what they are.
entries.subject: a safari vehicle beside lions in the Sabi Sands at dusk

entries.caption: The Drakensberg
entries.description: The Amphitheatre wall runs five kilometres and drops a kilometre, with San rock art in the caves beneath it.
entries.subject: the Amphitheatre wall of the Drakensberg escarpment

entries.caption: Tugela, Off the Amphitheatre
entries.description: Nearly a thousand metres in five leaps off the Drakensberg escarpment — among the highest falls on earth.
entries.subject: the Tugela Falls dropping off the Drakensberg Amphitheatre

entries.caption: Blyde River Canyon
entries.description: The third largest canyon in the world and the greenest, with the Three Rondavels standing in the middle of it.
entries.subject: the Three Rondavels above the Blyde River Canyon

entries.caption: Two Oceans
entries.description: Cold Atlantic on one side of the Cape peninsula, warm Indian on the other, forty minutes apart.
entries.subject: Camps Bay beach beneath the Twelve Apostles in Cape Town

entries.caption: Tsitsikamma
entries.description: Old yellowwood forest running down to a rocky coast, with the Storms River mouth cut through the middle.
entries.subject: the Storms River mouth suspension bridge in Tsitsikamma

entries.caption: Bloukrans and the Cage
entries.description: The highest commercial bridge bungee in the world, and great white cage diving out of Gansbaai.
entries.subject: the Bloukrans bridge bungee jump on the Garden Route

entries.caption: Eleven Languages
entries.description: Zulu, Xhosa, Afrikaans and eight more, plus the Cape Malay cooking that came with the slave trade.
entries.subject: Zulu dancers in traditional dress in KwaZulu-Natal

entries.caption: Zulu, Xhosa, Ndebele
entries.description: Ndebele wall painting, Zulu beadwork with its own grammar, and Xhosa initiation still practised in the Eastern Cape.
entries.subject: an Ndebele woman in beaded dress before a painted house wall

entries.caption: Braai, Bunny Chow, Curry
entries.description: Fire is a national institution; Durban curry and Cape Malay bobotie came from two very different arrivals.
entries.subject: meat over the coals at a South African braai

entries.caption: Carnival and AfrikaBurn
entries.description: The Cape Town Carnival in March, the Kaapse Klopse minstrels in January, and AfrikaBurn out in the Karoo.
entries.subject: performers in costume at the Cape Town Carnival

entries.caption: Ndebele Beadwork
entries.description: Beadwork, wire sculpture and telephone-wire baskets, sold everywhere and made properly in very few places.
entries.subject: Ndebele beadwork and geometric wall painting

entries.caption: Robben Island
entries.description: Twelve kilometres off Cape Town, a political prison for three decades, now guided by the men who were held there.
entries.subject: the prison buildings on Robben Island with Table Mountain behind

entries.caption: The Cradle of Humankind
entries.description: The Sterkfontein caves have produced more early hominin fossils than any other site on the planet.
entries.subject: the limestone caves of the Cradle of Humankind at Sterkfontein

entries.caption: Cape Town and Johannesburg
entries.description: One built around a mountain and a harbour, the other on a gold reef, and nothing about them is alike.
entries.subject: the Johannesburg skyline seen across the city at dusk

entries.caption: Bo-Kaap and Cape Dutch
entries.description: Painted Bo-Kaap terraces on the slope of Signal Hill, and gabled Cape Dutch homesteads out in the winelands.
entries.subject: the painted houses of the Bo-Kaap below Signal Hill

entries.caption: Soweto, Sunday
entries.description: Vilakazi Street, the shisa nyama grills, and a township of a million people that runs at its own pace.
entries.subject: a shisa nyama street grill in Soweto on a Sunday

entries.caption: Township Tourism, Done Right
entries.description: Guided by residents, spending in the neighbourhood, and honest about what apartheid planning actually built.
entries.subject: a resident guide leading a walking tour in Soweto

entries.caption: Lion's Head at Dawn
entries.description: Ninety minutes up a spiral path with chains near the top, for the whole peninsula at sunrise.
entries.subject: walkers on the spiral path up Lion's Head above Cape Town

entries.caption: The Winelands
entries.description: Franschhoek and Stellenbosch: Cape Dutch estates, serious kitchens, and a wine tram that means nobody drives.
entries.subject: a Cape Dutch wine estate among vineyards in Franschhoek

entries.caption: Marine and Rhino Work
entries.description: Whale watching at Hermanus, penguins at Boulders, and rhino monitoring in the reserves that fund it.
entries.subject: African penguins on the boulders at Simon's Town

entries.caption: Chapman's Peak Drive
entries.description: Nine kilometres cut into the cliff between Hout Bay and Noordhoek, and every turnout is a photograph.
entries.subject: Chapman's Peak Drive cut into the cliffs above the Atlantic

entries.caption: The Wild Coast and Karoo
entries.description: Hole in the Wall and the Transkei green hills, and the Karoo's enormous silence in the other direction.
entries.subject: the Hole in the Wall rock arch on the Wild Coast

entries.caption: Two Weeks, Four Countries' Worth
entries.description: Mountain, desert, reef, bush and two of Africa's most interesting cities, on roads you can drive yourself.
entries.subject: Cape Point where the two oceans meet at the tip of the peninsula
